# GridGame Gaiden — User Stories (parity backlog)

> One line per [BIBLE](BIBLE.md) mechanic or feature. Goal: **full parity** with the GridGame2026
> bible as amended in [AMENDMENTS.md](AMENDMENTS.md).
>
> Status: **✅ verified** — a named test in `Tests/Core.Tests` or an automation-harness step
> (`tools/harness.py smoke|sweep`) demonstrates it · **🟡 partial** — built (or partly built) but no
> test/harness step asserts the behavior, or the assertion is only indirect · **⬜ planned** — not
> built. For Camp screens, harness ✅ means "the screen builds, is screenshotted and layout-audited
> in `sweep`"; the service behind it has its own line.
>
> Evidence key: test names are NUnit methods in `Tests/Core.Tests/*.cs` (last run 2026-10-09: all
> green); **soak** = `ContentAndSoakTests.Bots_play_every_stage_without_breaking_invariants` (runs
> the mechanic over real content but asserts only invariants); **smoke** / **sweep** = harness runs
> whose artifacts are in `artifacts/smoke1/` and `artifacts/sweep/`.

## Definition of Done (every story)
1. `pwsh tools/test.ps1` green (and `-Compile` for App changes). 2. Bible section updated. 3. A named
test for every rule. 4. A harness step for anything visible. 5. Glyph check green. 6. One commit at the end.

| GG-T20 | 2026-10-13 | fix | closed | **Root cause of GG-T16, found and fixed.** Not an Input System or UI Toolkit staleness bug as first suspected — a plain confirm-dialog lifecycle bug, real for actual players too, not just automation. `Confirm.Show()` (`MenuScreens.cs`) adds its "veil" directly to the persistent `GameApp.Overlay` root, which `ScreenRouter` never touches — so if the screen changes (any `Push`/`Replace`/`ResetTo`, including the automation's `newgame` endpoint bypassing the UI entirely) while a confirm is showing and was never explicitly answered, the veil is orphaned: a full-screen `PickingMode.Position` layer that silently eats every future click forever, with zero error anywhere, since nothing ever told it to go away. This exactly explains every observed symptom: fine on a fresh launch, breaks after enough interactions (more chances to leave one stranded), both `click`-by-name and raw coordinate `tap` equally dead (the veil, not a missing/wrong target, ate the click), and killing the process always "fixes" it (a fresh process has no orphaned veil). Fixed by tagging the veil (`confirm-veil`) and having `ScreenRouter.Go()` dismiss any stale one on every navigation (`Confirm.DismissStale()`) before proceeding. Reproduced the exact original failure (automation `newgame` after an unanswered confirm → `clicktext("Adventure")` replies `ok:true` but screen stays on `hub`) against the pre-fix build, then confirmed the identical sequence against the fixed build correctly transitions to `stages`. Full dotnet suite green (370/370), Unity build clean. | full dotnet suite, live repro (`clicktext("Adventure")` after `newgame` bypass: stuck on pre-fix build, transitions correctly on fixed build) |
| GG-T19 | 2026-10-13 | fix | closed | Mitigation for GG-T16 (root cause still open): (1) `AutomationServer`'s `click` endpoint queried `Stage.Q(name)` with no visibility check at all, unlike `clicktext`'s `Query<>()` which already checked `display`/`worldBound.width` — added the same check (plus the existing `Opaque()` helper) so a hidden/zero-size/mid-transition match now returns a clear error instead of a false `ok:true`. (2) `tools/harness.py campaign()` now verifies a `click(name="next")`/`Continue` actually left the `postbattle` screen before moving on, retrying up to 5 times and then stopping the run cleanly with a clear message — instead of silently looping on a dead click for the rest of the run and reporting a stack of identical frozen "postbattle" results as if 20 stages had been played (exactly what happened in this session's `continue3.log`). Verified: full dotnet suite green (370/370), Unity build clean, a quick `tools/harness.py smoke` run still zero-errors. Does not fix the underlying Unity-side unresponsiveness (GG-T16 stays open) — makes the harness fail loudly and stop instead of silently fabricating a false "it worked" report. | full dotnet suite, `tools/harness.py smoke` |

| GG-T16 | 2026-10-13 | fix | closed | Root-caused and fixed by GG-T20 (below) — `AutomationServer`'s `click`/`clicktext` endpoints are intermittently unreliable over a long-running session: a `click(name=...)` or `clicktext(...)` call returns `{"ok": true}` with plausible design-space coordinates, but the tap doesn't register — the screen never advances, repeatably, across many retries, with no error anywhere (confirmed: tried raw `tap` at the same coordinates, tried a different button entirely, both equally unresponsive while stuck). Reproduced 3 separate times this session, always after substantial prior automation traffic in the same player process (never on a freshly-launched instance's first few interactions). Not root-caused: `Tap()`'s `InputSystem.QueueStateEvent` is frame-based not time-based, speed-of-game-simulation doesn't obviously explain it, and `runInBackground: 1` is already set so OS focus loss shouldn't matter. Workaround used this session: kill and relaunch the player process, which reliably clears it. Worth investigating: whether Unity's `InputSystem` virtual mouse device needs periodic re-registration, whether UI Toolkit's panel/EventSystem can get into a state where it stops dispatching pointer events, or whether there's unbounded state (timeline icons, FX layer children, etc.) accumulating over a long session that eventually blocks input processing. | GG-T67 | 2026-10-15 | fix | closed | Investigated GG-T21 with a new tools/harness.py stress HOURS command (launches once, keeps generating random battles via the randombattle endpoint, and polls the OS process directly with Popen.poll() every iteration instead of only noticing trouble through a failed/hung HTTP call). A 5h unattended run died after ~5 minutes (10 clips) -- but Player.log showed a clean Application.Quit() shutdown sequence (MindAttic.Capture CaptureRunner.OnQuitting -> physics/input-system teardown -> PlayerConnection::Cleanup), not a crash: nothing in this run's own code ever called quit. Root cause: harness.py's automation port defaulted to the same fixed 7787 for every GridGameGaiden git worktree, and launch() unconditionally quits whatever is already listening there before launching its own player -- so a second agent starting a harness run in a sibling worktree silently terminates a first agent's unrelated long-running session, with zero crash/exception trail from the terminated process's point of view. This repo explicitly expects concurrent multi-worktree agents (AGENTS.md); GG-T17's own concurrent harness run was independently found using a manually-chosen non-default port (17817), suggesting other agents had already informally worked around this. Separately, by code inspection: tools/deploy.ps1 stopped any process literally named GridGameGaiden with Stop-Process -Force, not scoped to its own worktree's Build output -- running /deploy from any worktree would forcibly kill any other worktree's running dev player too, and a hard kill leaves no app-level log output at all (no shutdown sequence, log just stops), which matches GG-T21's original symptom ("the log just stops mid-entry") even more closely than the port-collision mechanism caught live here. This doesn't retroactively prove deploy.ps1 caused the original ~1h incident -- no log survives from that session to confirm -- but it is a concrete, verified, same-shaped hazard in this repo's own tooling, strictly more likely than an undiagnosable engine crash, and worth fixing regardless. Fixed both: harness.py now derives its default automation port from a hash of the worktree's own path (GAIDEN_PORT still overrides), so sibling worktrees no longer collide by default; deploy.ps1 now scopes its Stop-Process to only processes whose exe path is under this repo's own Build\ output or the shared C:\Apps\GridGameGaiden\ deploy target. Also fixed a bug in the new stress() command itself where an HTTP call not immediately preceded by a Popen.poll() check could raise an uncaught exception instead of writing a clean crash-report.txt on an actual process death. Verified: full dotnet suite green (370/370), Unity build clean, tools/harness.py smoke clean (zero errors) against the new per-worktree port. | tools/harness.py smoke (clean, zero errors); full dotnet suite 370/370 |

| GG-T83 | 2026-10-16 | docs | open | Research spike (paused, unresolved): what topology should the unified build-a-character skill map actually have. Owner rejected three sketched approaches in a row; this records all of them plus two real-game references so a future session doesn't re-derive them from scratch. (A) Six independent trees + toll-gated bridge (original GG-T51 draft): home tree free, off-tree nodes cost a surcharge once a points threshold is met. Rejected: felt like a tax, not organic. (B) One connected hex map, 6 wedges meeting at a center, no toll, cost = path length (GG-T79, closed wont-do): still read as 'trees by archetype' just relabeled as wedges; its own opposite-pair claims (Guardian vs Mage as the longest walk) didn't even match its stated ring order, a real math error caught mid-session, not just a design miss. (C) Octagon of the game's 8 real stats (STR/VIT/AGI/SPD/STA/INT/WIS/LCK) with archetype clusters positioned by their primary/secondary stat pair, no walls between clusters: broke because forcing 8 stats onto a PoE-style shape doesn't match how PoE's tree actually works (only 3 attributes there), and produced a lopsided layout (Warrior isolated) nobody aimed for. (D) Archetype wheel, owner's own sketch: 8 'pure' archetypes (Warrior/Tank/Healer/Mage[added by Claude, not confirmed]/Debuffer/Buffer/Ranger/Thief) in a ring with 8 named hybrid nodes at the seams (Warrior x Tank, Tank x Healer, etc). Closest to what the owner wants but still called 'not quite right' -- Mage's placement in particular is an open question. Two real references surfaced but not yet applied: FF12 Zodiac Job System (12 separate per-job License Boards; a character dual-classes by picking exactly 2 of the 12 whole boards -- identity is which two boards, not where you walked) and FFX Sphere Grid (one shared lattice board everyone walks on from a different starting point, no drawn regions or walls at all -- structurally the closest real precedent to what's being searched for). Open question for next session: one shared walkable board with no drawn regions (Sphere-Grid-style), discrete per-archetype boards combined by picking two (Zodiac-style), or a named ring of pure+hybrid archetypes (owner's own wheel, option D, if refined). The class/region audit findings (GG-T80/81/82: Warrior overloaded, Guardian's Deathguard orphaned, Ranger has branches but no classes) remain valid and actionable under any of these topologies and don't need to wait on this decision. | owner direction 2026-10-16: paused research spike, revisit later |

| GG-T85 | 2026-10-16 | feature | open | Only 18 relic/trinket items exist in the entire game (items.json, Slot==Relic1, the generic relic marker Equipment.Fits lets into any of Relic1-3) -- not the ~128 an owner might expect for a 5-hero party each wanting 3 distinct relics (15 relic-slots to fill at once) across a 64-class roster. This is a real content shortage, not a code gap: the Relic1-in-any-slot mechanism (bible SS24.2) already works, there just isn't enough content to fill it meaningfully. Needs a real content-authoring pass: design and add relic/trinket ItemDefs with distinct passive effects (stat bonuses, on-hit procs, resistance mods -- same shape as the 4 existing named Epic+ passives PincerDamageBonus/RegenPerTurn/StartsProtected) until there's enough variety for real build diversity, not just 18 picked from repeatedly. | found during owner-requested gameplay/bug audit 2026-10-16; owner expectation of ~128 trinkets |
| GG-T86 | 2026-10-16 | feature | open | No unarmed-combat mechanic exists despite several unarmed-flavored classes. WeaponPower (Formulas.cs: off = Strength + WeaponPower) is a flat additive term that is exactly 0 with no weapon equipped (BattleRunner.Setup.cs sets it only inside 'if (weapon != null)', confirmed by direct read) -- no multiplier, no floor, no compensation. Worse, there is no Fist/Gauntlet/Glove WeaponType among the 10 that exist (Axe/Bow/Dagger/Greatsword/Hammer/Mace/Spear/Staff/Sword/Wand), so monk, martialartist, pugilist and streetfighter -- all explicitly built around unarmed/martial-arts flavor in their class identity and signature moves (martialartist_palm, pugilist_jabcross, monk_peace) -- have no thematically-appropriate weapon to equip and are mechanically just as incentivized to carry a sword as anyone else. Needs a design decision + build: either a baseline 'unarmed' WeaponPower floor scaled by a stat (STR or AGI), a new Fist/Gauntlet WeaponType with its own light itemDefs, and/or an Unarmed Mastery passive for these specific classes that makes fighting bare-handed competitive rather than strictly worse. | found during owner-requested gameplay/bug audit 2026-10-16 |
| GG-T87 | 2026-10-16 | fix | open | CampRoutine (Meta/CampRoutine.cs, the 'sensible player' automation BalanceReport and the soak suite drive) never calls Summon.Recruit or any Bounties.* method -- confirmed by direct grep, zero matches. The Summon Circle and Bounty Board are both fully built, player-facing Camp services, but no automated full-playthrough or balance test has ever exercised either of them as part of organic progression -- only one-off tests that call them directly and manually (e.g. Full_loop_battle_commit_then_every_vendor touches every vendor once, not as part of a played-out campaign). This means nobody has machine-verified that a real playthrough that recruits heroes or claims bounties as it goes still balances and completes the campaign the way CampRoutine already proves for gear/potions/skill-learning. Extend CampRoutine.Run to recruit from the Summon Circle when affordable and a party slot is open, and to accept/claim bounties when none is active, then rerun BalanceReport.Campaign_pacing_table to confirm the campaign still completes with these two systems actually in the loop. | found during owner-requested full-playthrough gameplay-loop audit 2026-10-16 |
